We tested our drone in the institute's lab. A thing the size of a big cat, basically a very smart quadcopter with good sensors.
We set it a task: fly from point A to point B dodging sudden obstacles. Charged it, launched it, it flew, successfully dodged our hands and flying objects along the way. Hovered at point B.
We went to turn it off, but it won't come to hand: it dodges obstacles (our hands) and returns to point B. We resigned ourselves, started waiting for the batteries to die. Didn't catch it with a net: could damage the props.
Waited and waited. The batteries are good: very expensive. And then something hit it in the head, and the drone flew off somewhere toward the study corridors. On one hand — let it fly, it won't hit anyone (we didn't even catch it on purpose). On the other — a crazy expensive machine flying off into the unknown...
In short we grabbed a net (a regular net, like for big fish) and the four of us ran to catch the monster. In front ran the electronics guy, dispersing people and trying to press the power stop, behind him the mechanic, lamenting "just don't break my precious's rotors", at the very back the programmers were busily dragging the net. Turns out the drone wanted to fly to the dean's office. Almost at the dean's office its batteries died, the programmers managed to hold the net under it, no one was hurt.
Since then we close the doors. And why a little net appeared on the windows — that's another story.
